title: Whitespace, Comments, Strings, and Line Numbers
description: The Model 2 lexer: skip whitespace with t_ignore, consume newlines and track line numbers, discard comments, strip quotes from strings, and report errors with a line number.

steps.description: This is the second lexer, which handles whitespace, comments, and strings. The page says every real source file contains text the parser should never see, and a lexer must consume it without leaking junk tokens. `t_ignore` skips spaces and tabs.

`t_NEWLINE` matches one or more newlines and adds their count to `t.lexer.lineno`. There is no return statement, so the token is consumed but not emitted. The page says PLY does not manage line numbers for you; you maintain them with `t.lexer.lineno`.

`t_COMMENT` matches a `#` and the rest of the line. `pass` returns `None` implicitly, so the comment is discarded. The page says a function rule that returns `None` consumes the token without emitting it.
`t_STRING` matches a double-quoted string and strips the surrounding quotes before returning. The page lists this as the third mechanism: modify `t.value` before returning.
`t_NUMBER` converts the matched number to a float. `t_ID` matches an identifier and checks `reserved`, promoting reserved words to their own type.

`t_error` reports an illegal character with its line. The last lines tokenize a multi-line source that has a full-line comment, an inline comment, and a string, and print each token's line, type, and value.
